questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Exchange was mandatory as part of the curriculum on my education. Due to the covid-pandemic between 2020-2023, UCPH has not able to send student on obligatory exchange with previously partnered universities in China, and had established a pilot program with a university in Taipei, Taiwan, for my class.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
My class was told shortly after enrollment (fall 2021), that the previous class had not been able to do the mandatory exchange with partnered universities due to at the time ongoing covid-pandemic. This resulted in the previous class being forced to follow the protocol curriculum of having comparable lectures at UCPH. Due to the evolving circumstances in relation to the covid-pandemic, we were told to prepare for the same treatment. Shortly after my class' 2. semester had begun, we were invited to a breifing from the UCPH Outgoing Exchange Office, who had initiated a pilot exchange program with new universities. The briefing was inchoate, but provided the bare necessary information and application deadlines for the obligatory exchange to be succesful. The following months were filled with chaotic messages and misunderstandings between my class and the Outgoing Exchange Office, as the Outgoing Exchange Office had failed to communicate sufficient information from the Taiwanese Trade Office, who had supreme authority on the matter (possible/impossible). The misunderstandings were solved by the students, and the pilot exchange was still afloat, provided that students were in direct contact with the Taiwanese Trade Office. 

Due to the circumstances of the covid-pandemic, the pilot exchange was always subject to potential changes, and put a lot of mental stress on students, ranging from uncertain housing situations to unclear transactional possibilities. No instruments for solving these issues were introduced to students by the UCPH Outgoing Exchange Office, who were solely responsible for matters related to the exchange spot on the host university. The majority of the class' students were able to overcome these issues, me included.

The duration and quality of the stay good, provided that the students themselves had taken measures to ensure this. No follow-up was initiated by the UCPH Outgoing Exchange Office for at least a month into the stay. The follow-up had no substantial information to provide. All communication with the host university was done more or less by students, which involved everything from credit transfers to whether the class was following the correct studyprogram. 

Credit transfer became an issue upon return, as the Credit Transfers Office under the UCPH Education and Student Office was unable to confirm the credit papers from the host university. The UCPH Outgoing Exchange Office did not provide any help on the issue.

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.answer: I rented an apartment from a private provider not associated with UCPH or the Taiwanese Ministry of Education.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Research the possibilities a fair amount of time in advance, as confirmed housing and the duration is necessary for doing exchange in Taiwan.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My housing situation was solely solved by own initiative.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The UCPH Outgoing Exchange Office was responsible for course registrations, but did not keep track on whether the host university was following the correct instructions.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After the application was sent by the UCPH Outgoing Exchange Office and confirmed by the host university, the host mandated a test for the each student to see which class we were supposed to follow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The host university allowed students to reapply for other classes in a transfer window, in case the students were unhappy with their current class.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: My designated classes were fine, as the host university were good at counselling me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If going on mandatory exchange, become aware of your rights at your host university, as you can not rely on the UCPH Outgoing Exchange Office to keep you informed.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fair, it very much depends on the individual on how much you want to adjust. I had little to no issues provided I had necessary information

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Stay in dialogue with other exchange students (known and unknown) and do non-academic activites with them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Garbage dispossal and non-insulated living facilities (the winter was particularly cold during my stay).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and night life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Appreciate it while on exchange, take care and responsibility for yourself, and don't rely on UCPH to make obligatory exchange an enjoyable experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Again, DO NOT rely on UCPH to make obligatory exchange an enjoyable experience. Talk with others who have had encounters with studying abroad.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The amount of knowledge I have obtained about a foreign culture (language, customs and general life).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Language barriers who can only my lessened by the amount of time invested in learning it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: DO NOT RELY ON UCPH TO MAKE OBLIGATORY EXCAHNGE AN ENJOYABLE EXPERIENCE!!!
